bull.t: Attruby revenue growth & high gross margins
bull.b: Sustained, rapid Attruby revenue growth combined with an approximately 95% gross margin creates a durable, high-quality cash margin on incremental sales. That scalable commercial economics support lasting operating leverage as launches and uptake continue, improving the path to breakeven.

bull.t: Multiple late-stage programs in regulatory review
bull.b: A diversified near-term approval slate reduces binary risk and expands addressable revenue beyond a single product. Multiple NDAs and priority reviews create staggered launch windows and de‑risk commercialization cadence, supporting more predictable multi-product growth over the next 2–18 months.

A large, structured preferred equity infusion materially extends runway and funds simultaneous launches without immediate common dilution. The capital is senior and permanent in design, reducing near-term refinancing risk and enabling continued investment in commercial scale and late‑stage programs.

bear.b: A sizable negative equity balance reflects accumulated losses and weak capital reserves, constraining financial flexibility. Over the medium term this heightens dilution or financing risk if launches or approvals falter, and can limit strategic optionality versus better‑capitalized peers.

Sustained large negative operating and free cash flow indicates dependence on external capital despite recent financing. Continued multi‑product launch spending and elevated opex mean cash consumption remains structural in the near term, raising execution risk if commercial ramps underdeliver.

A failed combination trial undermines the strategy of additive approaches and creates uncertainty about comparative positioning versus RNA knockdown competitors. This outcome may require reprioritization of R&D spend and lengthen timelines to prove long‑term clinical differentiation.
